Okny Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Okny, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, though it appears on Russian maps from 1914 and 1916-17, with its earliest ESJF-found gravestone dating to the 1860s, suggesting 19th-century operation; it was likely demolished after WWII, and since 1995 has been almost fully destroyed, with nearly all gravestones gone. Okny's Jewish community is first mentioned in the late 19th century, though population reached 182 as early as 1847; an 1882 pogrom struck the community, which supported three synagogues by 1889. Population reached 1,530 (63%) by 1897, with trade as the most common occupation; a Soviet-era peak of 1,972 came in 1926, with many families later joining kolkhozes or communes in the 1930s. Population fell to 1,258 (27%) by 1939. Wehrmacht occupation from August 7, 1941 saw 290 local Jews murdered by October, while more than 2,000 additional Jews were deported to Dubossary in Transnistria and murdered that September.
